bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Numbers

When asking **is 80k a good salary in australia**, it helps to start with the basics. The standard full-time week in Australia is 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. To convert an hourly rate to annual pay, multiply by hours per week and then by 52 weeks. For example, $40 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $79,040, very close to $80,000.

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees get an extra 25% loading, making the minimum $33.05 per hour. At $80,000 a year, you earn well above these minimums.

## Is $80k a Good Salary in Australia?

The answer depends on your industry, location, and lifestyle. Compared to the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (about $108,352 per year) from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, $80,000 is below average. However, it is above the median for all employees, which includes part-time workers. Many Australians earn less than $80,000, especially outside major cities or in entry-level roles.

$80,000 also puts you in the 30% tax bracket for 2026–27 (income between $45,001 and $135,000). After tax and the 2% Medicare levy, your take-home pay would be roughly $62,000 per year, or about $1,192 per week. This is a comfortable income for a single person in most areas, though housing costs in Sydney or Melbourne may stretch it.

## How to Convert Hourly to Annual

To find your annual salary from an hourly rate, use this formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross pay**

Assuming a 38-hour week, $80,000 per year gives an hourly rate of about $40.49. If you work fewer hours, your annual pay will be lower. For example, 30 hours per week at $40.49 would be about $63,164 per year.

You can also think in fortnights: weekly pay × 2. At $80,000 annually, weekly pay is about $1,538, so fortnightly is about $3,076 before tax. This helps when budgeting for bills or rent.

## Tax and Super Considerations

Your employer must pay superannuation on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830. So on $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 to your super account each year. This is not part of your take-home pay but is a valuable benefit.

Tax for 2026–27 uses these resident rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low incomes). For $80,000, your tax is about $16,267 plus Medicare of $1,600, leaving around $62,133 after tax.

## Award Rates and Annualised Wages

If you are covered by a modern award, your minimum pay may be higher than the National Minimum Wage. Awards set specific rates for classifications, plus penalties for overtime, weekends, and public holidays. Some awards allow annualised wages, where you receive a flat salary that covers these extras. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that an annualised wage must not be less than what you would have earned under the award.

Casual employees get a 25% loading on top of the base rate. If you are casual and earn $80,000, your base hourly rate would be about $32.39 before loading, which is below the casual minimum of $33.05. So $80,000 as a casual would be below the legal minimum if you work 38 hours. Always check your award or agreement.

## Final Thoughts

So, is 80k a good salary in australia? It is a solid income, above the minimum wage and enough for a comfortable lifestyle in most areas. It is below the full-time average but still puts you in the middle of the income distribution.
